# camel_language_rhai - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camel-language-rhai/0.22.0/camel_language_rhai/

## Expand description

camel-language-rhai — Rhai script language for Camel Rust.

Main types: `RhaiLanguage`, `RhaiExpression`, `RhaiPredicate`, `RhaiMutatingExpression`.
Scripts have access to `body`, `headers`, `header()`, `set_header()`, `property()`, `set_property()`.

[§](https://docs.rs#resource-limits)Resource Limits

Scripts are bounded by configurable limits sourced from `[languages.rhai.limits]`
in `Camel.toml`. When absent, the rust-camel runtime defaults apply:

| Limit | Default |
|---|---|
| `max-operations` | 100,000 |
| `max-string-size` | 1 MiB |
| `max-array-size` | 10,000 elements |
| `max-map-size` | 10,000 entries |
| `max-expression-depth` | 64 |
| `max-function-expression-depth` | 32 |
| `execution-timeout-ms` | 5,000 |

Every limit is `Option<_>`; `None` means “use rust-camel runtime default” (no
default-lie per ADR-0011).

[§](https://docs.rs#covered-threats)Covered threats

- Infinite loops (`loop {}`) — trip`max-operations`and`execution-timeout-ms`(whichever fires first).
- Oversized allocations — strings, arrays, maps each have size caps.
- Pathological nesting — expression and function-expression depths are bounded.

[§](https://docs.rs#timeout-caveat)Timeout caveat

`execution-timeout-ms` wraps `eval_with_scope` in `tokio::time::timeout` +
`spawn_blocking`. When the timeout fires, the route future resolves to an
error, but the blocking thread may continue executing until the script
trips `max-operations` or finishes. This is the same partial-mitigation
caveat shared with the Boa engine.

[§](https://docs.rs#sandboxing)Sandboxing

Rhai scripts **cannot access the host filesystem, network APIs, or Rhai
module loading**. This sandbox is **unconditional** — there is no config
opt-out.

Two structural layers enforce this:

- **Compile time**— the Rhai- `no_module`cargo feature (see root- `Cargo.toml`) disables module loading across the entire crate graph.
- **Runtime**— engines are built via- `Engine::new_raw()`plus an explicit- `StandardPackage`registration. Unlike- `Engine::new()`, this does not install a- `FileModuleResolver`.

Additionally, `eval` and `import` are registered as disabled symbols as
defense in depth (no-op safe if symbols are absent). If a future Rhai
package were to re-introduce module loading or dynamic evaluation, these
symbols would still be blocked to user scripts.

What the sandbox is **not**:

- It is not a CPU/memory cap. Those are separate resource limits; see rc-bpx.
- It does not block timing APIs (`sleep`,`timestamp`). Those remain part of`StandardPackage`; CPU/time-based DoS is covered by rc-bpx resource limits.
- It is not a side-channel defense (cache timing, memory layout). Out of scope.

If your integration genuinely needs filesystem or network access from a
route script, use the explicit Camel components (`file:`, `http:`) with
their own runtime policies — do not attempt to bypass this sandbox.

[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

- Resource limits (max operations, string/array/map sizes, expression
depths) are enforced as denial-of-service protection, not as a sandbox.
They are configurable — see [# Resource Limits](https://docs.rs#resource-limits)above.
- The `body`variable is always a string. Structured access to JSON/XML bodies requires explicit parsing within the script using Rhai’s built-in map/array types.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Rhai](https://docs.rs/struct.RhaiLanguage.html)- Language
- Rhai scripting language for rust-camel.

---

# sandogasa_koji - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sandogasa-koji/0.15.3/sandogasa_koji/

## Expand description

Koji build system CLI wrapper.

Provides functions for querying Koji tags and builds by shelling
out to the `koji` CLI. Supports multiple Koji profiles (e.g.
`cbs` for CentOS Build System).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [TagAdd](https://docs.rs/struct.TagAddEvent.html)- Event
- One “tagged into” event from `koji list-history --tag=<tag>`. Captures only the bits the activity-reporting code needs; the date column is parsed by the caller as needed.
- [Tagged](https://docs.rs/struct.TaggedBuild.html)- Build
- A build found in a Koji tag.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [build_](https://docs.rs/fn.build_creation_date.html)- creation_ - date
- Parse the build’s creation date from `koji buildinfo`.
- [build_](https://docs.rs/fn.build_info_with_changelog.html)- info_ - with_ - changelog
- Fetch `koji buildinfo --changelog <nvr>`output verbatim for display. Returns the raw stdout so callers can show it to a human reviewing the build. Errors propagate (unlike the date/rpm helpers, an unexpected failure here is worth surfacing during an interactive review).
- [build_](https://docs.rs/fn.build_rpms.html)- rpms
- List binary RPM names for a build via `koji buildinfo`.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_auth.html)- auth
- Verify an authenticated Koji session is available for `profile`by running`koji moshimoshi`(the authenticated hello).
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_tagged.html)- tagged
- List builds in a Koji tag with their owners.
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_tagged_nvrs.html)- tagged_ - nvrs
- List NVRs in a Koji tag (quiet mode, NVRs only).
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_tagged_package_names.html)- tagged_ - package_ - names
- List the latest source package names tagged into a Koji tag.
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_tags.html)- tags
- List Koji tag names matching a glob `pattern`(e.g.`hyperscale10s-*-release`). Wraps`koji list-tags <pattern>`.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_nvr.html)- nvr
- Parse an NVR string into (name, version, release).
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_nvr_name.html)- nvr_ - name
- Parse an NVR string into the package name.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_tag_history.html)- tag_ - history
- Parse `koji list-history`output and pick out only the “tagged into” entries. Format of those lines (as of koji 1.34,`--utc`):
- [regen_](https://docs.rs/fn.regen_repo.html)- repo
- Regenerate a Koji tag’s repo (`koji regen-repo --wait <tag>`).
- [tag_](https://docs.rs/fn.tag_build.html)- build
- Tag a build into a Koji tag (`koji tag-build --wait <tag> <nvr>`).
- [tag_](https://docs.rs/fn.tag_history.html)- history
- Walk a tag’s “tagged into” events in the window `[after, before)`and return them in chronological order. Implemented via`koji list-history --tag=<tag>`parsed line-by-line; only`tagged into`lines are kept (other event types like owner changes and untags are filtered out).
- [untag_](https://docs.rs/fn.untag_build.html)- build
- Untag a build from a Koji tag (`koji untag-build <tag> <nvr>`).

# hrdr_tools - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hrdr-tools/0.2.1/hrdr_tools/

## Expand description

`hrdr-tools` — the agentic tool set.

The locked MVP set: `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit`, `bash`, `grep`,
`glob`, `todo_write`. Each implements [ Tool](https://docs.rs/trait.Tool.html) and is exposed to the model
as a native OpenAI function. Efficiency is in the design: token-bounded
outputs, line-numbered reads for precise edits, ripgrep-backed search.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bash](https://docs.rs/struct.BashTool.html)- Tool
- [Checkpoint](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckpointInfo.html)- Info
- One revertible checkpoint (a turn that changed files).
- [Checkpoints](https://docs.rs/struct.Checkpoints.html)
- A disk-backed store of per-turn file pre-images.
- [Edit](https://docs.rs/struct.EditTool.html)- Tool
- [Glob](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobTool.html)- Tool
- [Grep](https://docs.rs/struct.GrepTool.html)- Tool
- [Guardrail](https://docs.rs/struct.Guardrail.html)
- One command rule: a regex matched against the whole shell command line and the corrective message returned to the model when it matches.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.Hook.html)
- One configured hook: run `run`(with`{path}`substituted) after tool`on`successfully mutates a file matching`glob`.
- [Power](https://docs.rs/struct.PowerShellTool.html)- Shell - Tool
- [Read](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadTool.html)- Tool
- [Todo](https://docs.rs/struct.TodoItem.html)- Item
- A single TODO item tracked by `todo_write`.
- [Todo](https://docs.rs/struct.TodoTool.html)- Tool
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolContext.html)- Context
- Shared execution context handed to every tool call.
- [Tool](https://docs.rs/struct.ToolRegistry.html)- Registry
- Ordered registry of tools, keyed by name.
- [WebFetch](https://docs.rs/struct.WebFetchTool.html)- Tool
- [WebSearch](https://docs.rs/struct.WebSearchTool.html)- Tool
- [Write](https://docs.rs/struct.WriteTool.html)- Tool

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS.html)- HOOK_ - TIMEOUT_ - MS
- Default per-hook timeout: formatters are fast; anything slower is stuck.
- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT.html)- MAX_ - OUTPUT
- Default cap on a single tool’s textual output, in bytes. Larger results are truncated with a marker so the model’s context is never blown by one call.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Tool](https://docs.rs/trait.Tool.html)
- A model-callable tool.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [available_](https://docs.rs/fn.available_shell_tools.html)- shell_ - tools
- The available shell tools for this machine (bash and/or PowerShell), only
including a tool when its interpreter is actually on `PATH`.
- [cap_](https://docs.rs/fn.cap_matches.html)- matches
- Cap search output at `max_matches`*matches*, appending a count of what was dropped and how to narrow the search. Only`path:NN:…`lines count as matches —`path-NN-…`context lines and`--`group separators (grep/rg`-C`format) ride along with their match, so a context-grep isn’t over-counted.
- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_guardrails.html)- guardrails
- First matching rule’s message, if `command`trips any guardrail. Quoted spans are blanked before matching so string*arguments*that merely mention a blocked command (e.g.`rg 'git add -A'`) don’t false-positive.
- [default_](https://docs.rs/fn.default_guardrails.html)- guardrails
- The built-in rules. Patterns are matched anywhere in the command string
(compound `a && b`commands included). Kept deliberately narrow: they block the exact foot-gun spellings, not whole subcommands.
- [floor_](https://docs.rs/fn.floor_char_boundary.html)- char_ - boundary
- Largest byte index `≤ max`that lies on a UTF-8 char boundary of`s`, so`&s[..floor_char_boundary(s, max)]`never panics on multibyte text. Returns`s.len()`when`max >= s.len()`. (std’s`str::floor_char_boundary`is still unstable, hence this helper.)
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_file_hooks.html)- file_ - hooks
- Run every hook matching (`tool`,`path`) sequentially, returning one warning line per hook that failed or timed out (empty = all quiet). Success output is discarded — the caller re-reads the file and diffs, so the model sees the effect, not the chatter.
- [truncate](https://docs.rs/fn.truncate.html)
- Truncate `text`to`max`bytes on a char boundary, appending a marker that tells the model output was cut.
- [truncate_](https://docs.rs/fn.truncate_inline.html)- inline
- Collapse `s`to a single line (newlines → spaces) and truncate to`max`**characters**, appending`…`if it was cut. For compact one-line previews (tool-arg previews, status lines) — width-based, unlike the byte-based`truncate`
- [truncate_](https://docs.rs/fn.truncate_middle.html)- middle
- Truncate to `max`bytes keeping the**head and tail**with the omission in the middle. For shell output: build/test runs put the errors at the end, so head-only truncation (plain`truncate`
- [unix_](https://docs.rs/fn.unix_now.html)- now
- Current Unix time in whole seconds (0 if the clock is before the epoch). Shared by checkpoint journaling and session metadata.

- A GitLab user as returned by `/users?username=<name>`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [count_](https://docs.rs/fn.count_authored_commits.html)- authored_ - commits
- Count commits in `project_id`authored by`author`within`[since, until]`(inclusive). GitLab’s commits endpoint matches the`author`parameter against both name and email fields, so passing the GitLab username usually works; if the user authored commits under an email only, pass that email string instead.
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_archived_project_names.html)- archived_ - project_ - names
- List the **archived**projects under a GitLab group, returning their names. GitLab’s`archived=true`filter narrows the listing server-side, so this is a cheap separate query rather than enriching every project in the main listing.
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_group_projects.html)- group_ - projects
- List all projects under a GitLab group (public, no auth needed).
- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_tags.html)- tags
- List tags for a project, paginated. Returns an empty list on
404. Uses `order_by=updated&sort=desc`so newer tags come first — handy when the caller wants to short-circuit on the first tag older than its window of interest.
- [package_](https://docs.rs/fn.package_from_issue_url.html)- from_ - issue_ - url
- Extract the package name from a GitLab issue or work item web_url.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_issue_url.html)- issue_ - url
- Parse a GitLab issue / work-item URL into its components.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/fn.parse_mr_url.html)- mr_ - url
- Parse a merge request URL into its components.

- Parse a GitLab project URL into (base_url, project_path).
- [project_](https://docs.rs/fn.project_path_from_issue_url.html)- path_ - from_ - issue_ - url
- Extract the project path from a GitLab issue or work item web_url.
- [project_](https://docs.rs/fn.project_releases.html)- releases
- List releases for a project. Returns an empty list on 404 (project gone) so callers can iterate over many projects without per-project error handling.
- [project_](https://docs.rs/fn.project_summary.html)- summary
- Look up a project’s `path_with_namespace`from its numeric ID. Used to map event`project_id`→ group-prefix filter.
- [user_](https://docs.rs/fn.user_by_username.html)- by_ - username
- Look up a user by username on a specific GitLab instance.
Returns `Ok(None)`if the server returns 200 with an empty list (no user with that name on that instance).
- [user_](https://docs.rs/fn.user_events.html)- events
- Fetch a user’s activity events within `[after, before)`— GitLab’s event endpoint is half-open on both sides and rejects both-null. Results are paginated at 100/page; this follows every page until a short page arrives.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_token.html)- token
- Check whether a token is valid by calling `GET /api/v4/user`.

# sandogasa_github - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sandogasa-github/0.15.3/sandogasa_github/

## Expand description

HTTP client for the GitHub REST API.

Scoped to the surface `sandogasa-report` needs for activity
reports: user identity lookup, token validation, paginated
user events (to find which repos a user touched in a window),
the Search API for pull requests, and per-repo
authored-commit counts.

Mirrors `sandogasa-gitlab` in shape so downstream tools can
treat the two forges the same way structurally — host-keyed
tokens and identities, optional org/group filter, etc.

```
use sandogasa_github::Client;
let client = Client::new("https://api.github.com", "ghp_token")?;
let user = client.user_by_username("octocat")?.expect("user exists");
let prs = client.search_pull_requests(
    &format!("type:pr author:{} created:2026-01-01..2026-03-31", user.login),
)?;
for pr in prs {
    println!("{}: {}", pr.number, pr.title);
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Annotated](https://docs.rs/struct.AnnotatedTag.html)- Tag
- An annotated-tag object from
`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/tags/{sha}`. Only annotated tags carry tagger metadata; lightweight tags don’t have an addressable tag object.
- [Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html)
- Blocking GitHub REST client.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.Event.html)
- One entry from `/users/{username}/events`. Fields are sparse; we keep just enough to identify the event type, associated repo, and the actor.
- [GitObject](https://docs.rs/struct.GitObject.html)
- The thing a Git ref points at. `object_type`is`"commit"`for lightweight tags and`"tag"`for annotated ones.
- [GitTag](https://docs.rs/struct.GitTagRef.html)- Ref
- One entry from `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/refs/tags`. The underlying`object`distinguishes lightweight tags (point directly to a commit) from annotated tags (point to a Tag object that carries tagger info).
- [Pull](https://docs.rs/struct.PullRequest.html)- Request
- A pull request as returned by the Search Issues endpoint
when filtering on `type:pr`. The Search API actually returns “issue” objects with PR-specific fields populated, so we shape this around the union of useful fields rather than the fuller`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}`model.
- [Pull](https://docs.rs/struct.PullRequestRef.html)- Request - Ref
- Auxiliary block on a search-result issue when it’s actually a pull request. The Search Issues endpoint signals “is PR” by populating this; merged state lives here too.
- [Repository](https://docs.rs/struct.Repository.html)
- A repository as returned by event payloads and PR responses.
- [Tagger](https://docs.rs/struct.Tagger.html)
- `name`+- `email`+- `date`triple stamped on annotated-tag creation.- `date`is ISO 8601 (e.g.- `2026-05-15T17:03:15Z`).
- [User](https://docs.rs/struct.User.html)
- A GitHub user as returned by `/users/{username}`. Only the fields downstream tools currently consume.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_BASE_URL.html)- BASE_ - URL
- Default production base URL for the GitHub REST API.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_token.html)- token
- Check whether `token`works against`base_url`by hitting`/user`. Returns`Ok(true)`for valid tokens,`Ok(false)`for 401s, and`Err`for other transport / server errors so callers can distinguish “tried and was rejected” from “couldn’t reach the server”.

---

# kanal 0.1.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/kanal/0.1.1

# Kanal

**The fast sync and async channel that Rust deserves!**

## What is Kanal

The Kanal library is a Rust implementation of channels inspired by the CSP (Communicating Sequential Processes) model. It aims to help programmers create efficient concurrent programs by providing multi-producer and multi-consumer channels with advanced features for fast communication. The library focuses on unifying message passing between synchronous and asynchronous parts of Rust code, offering a combination of synchronous and asynchronous APIs while maintaining high performance.

## Why Kanal is faster?

- Kanal employs a highly optimized composite technique for the transfer of objects. When the data size is less than or equal to the pointer size, it utilizes serialization, encoding the data as the pointer address. Conversely, when the data size exceeds the pointer size, the protocol employs a strategy similar to that utilized by the Golang programming language, utilizing direct memory access to copy objects from the sender's stack or write directly to the receiver's stack. This composite method not only eliminates unnecessary pointer access but also eliminates heap allocations for bounded(0) channels.
- Kanal utilizes a specially tuned mutex for its channel locking mechanism, made possible by the predictable internal lock time of the channel. That said it's possible to use Rust standard mutex with the `std-mutex`feature and Kanal will perform better than competitors with that feature too.
- Utilizing Rust high-performance compiler and powerful LLVM backend with highly optimized memory access and deeply thought algorithms.

## Usage

To use Kanal in your Rust project, add the following line to your `Cargo.toml` file:

```
[]
 = "0.1"
```
Sync channel example:

```
// Initialize a bounded sync channel with a capacity for 8 messages
let  = bounded;
let s = sender.clone;
spawn;
// Receive an example message in another thread
let msg = receiver.recv?;
println!;
// Convert and use channel in async context to communicate between sync and async
spawn;
```
Async channel example:

```
// Initialize a bounded channel with a capacity for 8 messages
let  = bounded_async;
sender.send.await?;
sender.send.await?;
// Clone receiver and convert it to a sync receiver
let receiver_sync = receiver.clone.to_sync;
spawn;
// Spawn a thread and use receiver in sync context
spawn;
```
## Why use Kanal?

- Kanal offers fast and efficient communication capabilities.
- Kanal simplifies communication in and between synchronous and asynchronous contexts, thanks to its flexible API like `as_sync`and`as_async`.
- Kanal provides a clean and intuitive API, making it easier to work with compared to other Rust libraries.
- Similar to Golang, Kanal allows you to close channels using the `Close`function, enabling you to broadcast a close signal from any channel instance and close the channel for both senders and receivers.
- Kanal includes high-performance MPMC (Multiple Producers Multiple Consumers) and SPSC (Single Producer Single Consumer) channels in a single package.

### Benchmark Results

Results are based on how many messages can be passed in each scenario per second.

#### Test types:

- Seq is sequentially writing and reading to a channel in the same thread.
- SPSC is one receiver, and one sender and passing messages between them.
- MPSC is multiple sender threads with only one receiver.
- MPMC is multiple senders and multiple receivers communicating through the same channel.

#### Message types:

- `usize`tests are transferring messages of size hardware pointer.
- `big`tests are transferring messages of 8x the size of the hardware pointer.

N/A means that the test subject is unable to perform the test due to its limitations, Some of the test subjects don't have implementation for size 0 channels, MPMC or unbounded channels.

Machine: `AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor`
Rust: `rustc 1.85.1 (4eb161250 2025-03-15)`
Go: `go version go1.24.1 linux/amd64`
OS (`uname -a`): `Linux 6.11.0-19-generic #19~24.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon Feb 17 11:51:52 UTC 2 x86_64`
Date: Mar 19, 2025

#### Why does async outperform sync in some tests?

In certain tests, asynchronous communication may exhibit superior performance compared to synchronous communication. This can be attributed to the context-switching performance of libraries such as tokio, which, similar to Golang, utilize context-switching within the same thread to switch to the next coroutine when a message is ready on a channel. This approach is more efficient than communicating between separate threads. This same principle applies to asynchronous network applications, which generally exhibit better performance compared to synchronous implementations. As the channel size increases, one may observe improved performance in synchronous benchmarks, as the sending threads are able to push data directly to the channel queue without requiring awaiting blocking/suspending signals from receiving threads.

# kanal - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/kanal/0.1.1/target-redirect/kanal/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#kanal)Kanal

**The fast sync and async channel that Rust deserves!**

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-kanal)What is Kanal

The Kanal library is a Rust implementation of channels inspired by the CSP (Communicating Sequential Processes) model. It aims to help programmers create efficient concurrent programs by providing multi-producer and multi-consumer channels with advanced features for fast communication. The library focuses on unifying message passing between synchronous and asynchronous parts of Rust code, offering a combination of synchronous and asynchronous APIs while maintaining high performance.

[§](https://docs.rs#why-kanal-is-faster)Why Kanal is faster?

- Kanal employs a highly optimized composite technique for the transfer of objects. When the data size is less than or equal to the pointer size, it utilizes serialization, encoding the data as the pointer address. Conversely, when the data size exceeds the pointer size, the protocol employs a strategy similar to that utilized by the Golang programming language, utilizing direct memory access to copy objects from the sender’s stack or write directly to the receiver’s stack. This composite method not only eliminates unnecessary pointer access but also eliminates heap allocations for bounded(0) channels.
- Kanal utilizes a specially tuned mutex for its channel locking mechanism, made possible by the predictable internal lock time of the channel. That said it’s possible to use Rust standard mutex with the `std-mutex`feature and Kanal will perform better than competitors with that feature too.
- Utilizing Rust high-performance compiler and powerful LLVM backend with highly optimized memory access and deeply thought algorithms.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

To use Kanal in your Rust project, add the following line to your `Cargo.toml` file:

```
[dependencies]
kanal = "0.1"
```
Sync channel example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// Initialize a bounded sync channel with a capacity for 8 messages
let (sender, receiver) = kanal::bounded(8);
let s = sender.clone();
std::thread::spawn(move || {
    s.send("hello")?;
    anyhow::Ok(())
});
// Receive an example message in another thread
let msg = receiver.recv()?;
println!("I got msg: {}", msg);
// Convert and use channel in async context to communicate between sync and async
tokio::spawn(async move {
    // Borrow the channel as an async channel and use it in an async context ( or convert it to async using to_async() )
    sender.as_async().send("hello").await?;
    anyhow::Ok(())
});
```
Async channel example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// Initialize a bounded channel with a capacity for 8 messages
let (sender, receiver) = kanal::bounded_async(8);
sender.send("hello").await?;
sender.send("hello").await?;
// Clone receiver and convert it to a sync receiver
let receiver_sync = receiver.clone().to_sync();
tokio::spawn(async move {
    let msg = receiver.recv().await?;
    println!("I got msg: {}", msg);
    anyhow::Ok(())
});
// Spawn a thread and use receiver in sync context
std::thread::spawn(move || {
    let msg = receiver_sync.recv()?;
    println!("I got msg in sync context: {}", msg);
    anyhow::Ok(())
});
```
[§](https://docs.rs#why-use-kanal)Why use Kanal?

- Kanal offers fast and efficient communication capabilities.
- Kanal simplifies communication in and between synchronous and asynchronous contexts, thanks to its flexible API like `as_sync`and`as_async`.
- Kanal provides a clean and intuitive API, making it easier to work with compared to other Rust libraries.
- Similar to Golang, Kanal allows you to close channels using the `Close`function, enabling you to broadcast a close signal from any channel instance and close the channel for both senders and receivers.
- Kanal includes high-performance MPMC (Multiple Producers Multiple Consumers) and SPSC (Single Producer Single Consumer) channels in a single package.

[§](https://docs.rs#benchmark-results)Benchmark Results

Results are based on how many messages can be passed in each scenario per second.

- MPSC is multiple sender threads with only one receiver.
- MPMC is multiple senders and multiple receivers communicating through the same channel.

[§](https://docs.rs#message-types)Message types:

- `big`tests are transferring messages of 8x the size of the hardware pointer.

- Error type for closing a channel when channel is already closed

- ReceiveFuture is a future for receiving an object from a channel asynchronously. It must be polled to complete the receive operation.
- [Receive](https://docs.rs/struct.ReceiveStream.html)- Stream
- ReceiveStream is a stream for receiving objects from a channel asynchronously.
- [Receiver](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)
- Receiving side of the channel in sync mode. Receivers can be cloned and produce receivers to operate in both sync and async modes.
- [Send](https://docs.rs/struct.SendFuture.html)- Future
- SendFuture is a future for sending an object to a channel asynchronously. It must be polled to complete the send operation.
- [Sender](https://docs.rs/struct.Sender.html)
- Sending side of the channel with sync API. It’s possible to convert it to
async `AsyncSender``as_async`,`to_async`or`clone_async`based on software requirement.

- Creates a new sync bounded channel with the requested buffer size, and
returns `Sender``Receiver``AsyncSender``AsyncReceiver``to_sync`,`as_async`or`clone_sync`based on your requirements, by calling them on sender or receiver.
- [bounded_](https://docs.rs/fn.bounded_async.html)- async
- Creates a new async bounded channel with the requested buffer size, and
returns `AsyncSender``AsyncReceiver``Sender``Receiver``to_sync`,`as_async`or`clone_sync`based on your requirements, by calling them on async sender or receiver.
- [unbounded](https://docs.rs/fn.unbounded.html)
- Creates a new sync unbounded channel, and returns `Sender``Receiver``AsyncSender``AsyncReceiver``to_sync`,`as_async`or`clone_sync`based on your requirements, by calling them on sender or receiver.
- [unbounded_](https://docs.rs/fn.unbounded_async.html)- async
- Creates a new async unbounded channel, and returns `AsyncSender``AsyncReceiver``Sender``Receiver``to_sync`,`as_async`or`clone_sync`based on your requirements, by calling them on async sender or receiver.

[51](https://docs.rs#51)/// Sending side of the channel with async API.  It's possible to convert it to
[52](https://docs.rs#52)/// sync [`Sender`] with `as_sync`, `to_sync` or `clone_sync` based on software
[53](https://docs.rs#53)/// requirement.
[54](https://docs.rs#54)///
[55](https://docs.rs#55)/// # Examples
[56](https://docs.rs#56)///
[57](https://docs.rs#57)/// ```
[58](https://docs.rs#58)/// let (sender, _r) = kanal::bounded_async::<u64>(0);
[59](https://docs.rs#59)/// let sync_sender=sender.clone_sync();
[60](https://docs.rs#60)/// ```
[61](https://docs.rs#61)#[cfg(feature = "async")]
[62](https://docs.rs#62)#[repr(C)]
[63](https://docs.rs#63)pub struct AsyncSender<T> {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)    internal: Internal<T>,
[65](https://docs.rs#65)}
[66](https://docs.rs#66)
[67](https://docs.rs#67)impl<T> Drop for Sender<T> {
[68](https://docs.rs#68)    fn drop(&mut self) {
[69](https://docs.rs#69)        let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[70](https://docs.rs#70)        if internal.send_count > 0 {
[71](https://docs.rs#71)            internal.send_count -= 1;
[72](https://docs.rs#72)            if internal.send_count == 0 && internal.recv_count != 0 {
[73](https://docs.rs#73)                internal.terminate_signals();
[74](https://docs.rs#74)            }
[75](https://docs.rs#75)        }
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    }
[77](https://docs.rs#77)}

[236](https://docs.rs#236)        /// Closes the channel completely on both sides and terminates waiting
[237](https://docs.rs#237)        /// signals.
[238](https://docs.rs#238)        ///
[239](https://docs.rs#239)        /// # Examples
[240](https://docs.rs#240)        ///
[241](https://docs.rs#241)        /// ```
[242](https://docs.rs#242)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::unbounded::<u64>();
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        /// // closes channel on both sides and has same effect as r.close();
[244](https://docs.rs#244)        /// s.close().unwrap();
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        /// assert_eq!(r.is_closed(),true);
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        /// assert_eq!(s.is_closed(),true);
[247](https://docs.rs#247)        /// ```
[248](https://docs.rs#248)        pub fn close(&self) -> Result<(), CloseError> {
[249](https://docs.rs#249)            let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[250](https://docs.rs#250)            if internal.recv_count == 0 && internal.send_count == 0 {
[251](https://docs.rs#251)                return Err(CloseError());
[252](https://docs.rs#252)            }
[253](https://docs.rs#253)            internal.recv_count = 0;
[254](https://docs.rs#254)            internal.send_count = 0;
[255](https://docs.rs#255)            internal.terminate_signals();
[256](https://docs.rs#256)            internal.queue.clear();
[257](https://docs.rs#257)            Ok(())
[258](https://docs.rs#258)        }
[259](https://docs.rs#259)        /// Returns whether the channel is closed on both side of send and
[260](https://docs.rs#260)        /// receive or not.
[261](https://docs.rs#261)        ///
[262](https://docs.rs#262)        /// # Examples
[263](https://docs.rs#263)        ///
[264](https://docs.rs#264)        /// ```
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::unbounded::<u64>();
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        /// // closes channel on both sides and has same effect as r.close();
[267](https://docs.rs#267)        /// s.close();
[268](https://docs.rs#268)        /// assert_eq!(r.is_closed(),true);
[269](https://docs.rs#269)        /// assert_eq!(s.is_closed(),true);
[270](https://docs.rs#270)        /// ```
[271](https://docs.rs#271)        pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
[272](https://docs.rs#272)            let internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[273](https://docs.rs#273)            internal.send_count == 0 && internal.recv_count == 0
[274](https://docs.rs#274)        }

[277](https://docs.rs#277)
[278](https://docs.rs#278)macro_rules! shared_send_impl {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    () => {
[280](https://docs.rs#280)        /// Tries sending to the channel without waiting on the waitlist, if
[281](https://docs.rs#281)        /// send fails then the object will be dropped. It returns `Ok(true)` in
[282](https://docs.rs#282)        /// case of a successful operation and `Ok(false)` for a failed one, or
[283](https://docs.rs#283)        /// error in case that channel is closed. Important note: this function
[284](https://docs.rs#284)        /// is not lock-free as it acquires a mutex guard of the channel
[285](https://docs.rs#285)        /// internal for a short time.
[286](https://docs.rs#286)        ///
[287](https://docs.rs#287)        /// # Examples
[288](https://docs.rs#288)        ///
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        /// ```
[290](https://docs.rs#290)        /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[291](https://docs.rs#291)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[292](https://docs.rs#292)        /// let t=spawn( move || {
[293](https://docs.rs#293)        ///     loop{
[294](https://docs.rs#294)        ///         if s.try_send(1).unwrap(){
[295](https://docs.rs#295)        ///             break;
[296](https://docs.rs#296)        ///         }
[297](https://docs.rs#297)        ///     }
[298](https://docs.rs#298)        /// });
[299](https://docs.rs#299)        /// assert_eq!(r.recv()?,1);
[300](https://docs.rs#300)        /// # t.join();
[301](https://docs.rs#301)        /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[302](https://docs.rs#302)        /// ```
[303](https://docs.rs#303)        #[inline(always)]
[304](https://docs.rs#304)        pub fn try_send(&self, data: T) -> Result<bool, SendError> {
[305](https://docs.rs#305)            let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[306](https://docs.rs#306)            if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[307](https://docs.rs#307)                let send_count = internal.send_count;
[308](https://docs.rs#308)                // Avoid wasting lock time on dropping failed send object
[309](https://docs.rs#309)                drop(internal);
[310](https://docs.rs#310)                if send_count == 0 {
[311](https://docs.rs#311)                    return Err(SendError::Closed);
[312](https://docs.rs#312)                }
[313](https://docs.rs#313)                return Err(SendError::ReceiveClosed);
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            }
[315](https://docs.rs#315)            if let Some(first) = internal.next_recv() {
[316](https://docs.rs#316)                drop(internal);
[317](https://docs.rs#317)                // Safety: it's safe to send to owned signal once
[318](https://docs.rs#318)                unsafe { first.send(data) }
[319](https://docs.rs#319)                return Ok(true);
[320](https://docs.rs#320)            } else if internal.queue.len() < internal.capacity {
[321](https://docs.rs#321)                internal.queue.push_back(data);
[322](https://docs.rs#322)                return Ok(true);
[323](https://docs.rs#323)            }
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            Ok(false)
[325](https://docs.rs#325)        }
[326](https://docs.rs#326)
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        /// Tries sending to the channel without waiting on the waitlist, if
[328](https://docs.rs#328)        /// send fails then the object will be dropped. It returns `Ok(true)` in
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        /// case of a successful operation and `Ok(false)` for a failed one, or
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        /// error in case that channel is closed. Important note: this function
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        /// is not lock-free as it acquires a mutex guard of the channel
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        /// internal for a short time.
[333](https://docs.rs#333)        ///
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        /// # Examples
[335](https://docs.rs#335)        ///
[336](https://docs.rs#336)        /// ```
[337](https://docs.rs#337)        /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[338](https://docs.rs#338)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        /// let t=spawn( move || {
[340](https://docs.rs#340)        ///     let mut opt=Some(1);
[341](https://docs.rs#341)        ///     loop{
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        ///         if s.try_send_option(&mut opt).unwrap(){
[343](https://docs.rs#343)        ///             break;
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        ///         }
[345](https://docs.rs#345)        ///     }
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        /// });
[347](https://docs.rs#347)        /// assert_eq!(r.recv()?,1);
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        /// # t.join();
[349](https://docs.rs#349)        /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        /// ```
[351](https://docs.rs#351)        #[inline(always)]
[352](https://docs.rs#352)        pub fn try_send_option(&self, data: &mut Option<T>) -> Result<bool, SendError> {
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            if data.is_none() {
[354](https://docs.rs#354)                panic!("send data option is None");
[355](https://docs.rs#355)            }
[356](https://docs.rs#356)            let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[357](https://docs.rs#357)            if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[358](https://docs.rs#358)                let send_count = internal.send_count;
[359](https://docs.rs#359)                // Avoid wasting lock time on dropping failed send object
[360](https://docs.rs#360)                drop(internal);
[361](https://docs.rs#361)                if send_count == 0 {
[362](https://docs.rs#362)                    return Err(SendError::Closed);
[363](https://docs.rs#363)                }
[364](https://docs.rs#364)                return Err(SendError::ReceiveClosed);
[365](https://docs.rs#365)            }
[366](https://docs.rs#366)            if let Some(first) = internal.next_recv() {
[367](https://docs.rs#367)                drop(internal);
[368](https://docs.rs#368)                // Safety: it's safe to send to owned signal once
[369](https://docs.rs#369)                unsafe { first.send(data.take().unwrap()) }
[370](https://docs.rs#370)                return Ok(true);
[371](https://docs.rs#371)            } else if internal.queue.len() < internal.capacity {
[372](https://docs.rs#372)                internal.queue.push_back(data.take().unwrap());
[373](https://docs.rs#373)                return Ok(true);
[374](https://docs.rs#374)            }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            Ok(false)
[376](https://docs.rs#376)        }
[377](https://docs.rs#377)
[378](https://docs.rs#378)        /// Tries sending to the channel without waiting on the waitlist or for
[379](https://docs.rs#379)        /// the internal mutex, if send fails then the object will be dropped.
[380](https://docs.rs#380)        /// It returns `Ok(true)` in case of a successful operation and
[381](https://docs.rs#381)        /// `Ok(false)` for a failed one, or error in case that channel is
[382](https://docs.rs#382)        /// closed. Do not use this function unless you know exactly what you
[383](https://docs.rs#383)        /// are doing.
[384](https://docs.rs#384)        ///
[385](https://docs.rs#385)        /// # Examples
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        ///
[387](https://docs.rs#387)        /// ```
[388](https://docs.rs#388)        /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[389](https://docs.rs#389)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[390](https://docs.rs#390)        /// let t=spawn( move || {
[391](https://docs.rs#391)        ///     loop{
[392](https://docs.rs#392)        ///         if s.try_send_realtime(1).unwrap(){
[393](https://docs.rs#393)        ///             break;
[394](https://docs.rs#394)        ///         }
[395](https://docs.rs#395)        ///     }
[396](https://docs.rs#396)        /// });
[397](https://docs.rs#397)        /// assert_eq!(r.recv()?,1);
[398](https://docs.rs#398)        /// # t.join();
[399](https://docs.rs#399)        /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[400](https://docs.rs#400)        /// ```
[401](https://docs.rs#401)        #[inline(always)]
[402](https://docs.rs#402)        pub fn try_send_realtime(&self, data: T) -> Result<bool, SendError> {
[403](https://docs.rs#403)            if let Some(mut internal) = try_acquire_internal(&self.internal) {
[404](https://docs.rs#404)                if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[405](https://docs.rs#405)                    let send_count = internal.send_count;
[406](https://docs.rs#406)                    // Avoid wasting lock time on dropping failed send object
[407](https://docs.rs#407)                    drop(internal);
[408](https://docs.rs#408)                    if send_count == 0 {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)                        return Err(SendError::Closed);
[410](https://docs.rs#410)                    }
[411](https://docs.rs#411)                    return Err(SendError::ReceiveClosed);
[412](https://docs.rs#412)                }
[413](https://docs.rs#413)                if let Some(first) = internal.next_recv() {
[414](https://docs.rs#414)                    drop(internal);
[415](https://docs.rs#415)                    // Safety: it's safe to send to owned signal once
[416](https://docs.rs#416)                    unsafe { first.send(data) }
[417](https://docs.rs#417)                    return Ok(true);
[418](https://docs.rs#418)                } else if internal.queue.len() < internal.capacity {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)                    internal.queue.push_back(data);
[420](https://docs.rs#420)                    return Ok(true);
[421](https://docs.rs#421)                }
[422](https://docs.rs#422)            }
[423](https://docs.rs#423)            Ok(false)
[424](https://docs.rs#424)        }
[425](https://docs.rs#425)
[426](https://docs.rs#426)        /// Tries sending to the channel without waiting on the waitlist or
[427](https://docs.rs#427)        /// channel internal lock. It returns `Ok(true)` in case of a successful
[428](https://docs.rs#428)        /// operation and `Ok(false)` for a failed one, or error in case that
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        /// channel is closed. This function will `panic` on successful send
[430](https://docs.rs#430)        /// attempt of `None` data. Do not use this function unless you know
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        /// exactly what you are doing.
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        ///
[433](https://docs.rs#433)        /// # Examples
[434](https://docs.rs#434)        ///
[435](https://docs.rs#435)        /// ```
[436](https://docs.rs#436)        /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[438](https://docs.rs#438)        /// let t=spawn( move || {
[439](https://docs.rs#439)        ///     let mut opt=Some(1);
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        ///     loop{
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        ///         if s.try_send_option_realtime(&mut opt).unwrap(){
[442](https://docs.rs#442)        ///             break;
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        ///         }
[444](https://docs.rs#444)        ///     }
[445](https://docs.rs#445)        /// });
[446](https://docs.rs#446)        /// assert_eq!(r.recv()?,1);
[447](https://docs.rs#447)        /// # t.join();
[448](https://docs.rs#448)        /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[449](https://docs.rs#449)        /// ```
[450](https://docs.rs#450)        #[inline(always)]
[451](https://docs.rs#451)        pub fn try_send_option_realtime(&self, data: &mut Option<T>) -> Result<bool, SendError> {
[452](https://docs.rs#452)            if data.is_none() {
[453](https://docs.rs#453)                panic!("send data option is None");
[454](https://docs.rs#454)            }
[455](https://docs.rs#455)            if let Some(mut internal) = try_acquire_internal(&self.internal) {
[456](https://docs.rs#456)                if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[457](https://docs.rs#457)                    let send_count = internal.send_count;
[458](https://docs.rs#458)                    // Avoid wasting lock time on dropping failed send object
[459](https://docs.rs#459)                    drop(internal);
[460](https://docs.rs#460)                    if send_count == 0 {
[461](https://docs.rs#461)                        return Err(SendError::Closed);
[462](https://docs.rs#462)                    }
[463](https://docs.rs#463)                    return Err(SendError::ReceiveClosed);
[464](https://docs.rs#464)                }
[465](https://docs.rs#465)                if let Some(first) = internal.next_recv() {
[466](https://docs.rs#466)                    drop(internal);
[467](https://docs.rs#467)                    // Safety: it's safe to send to owned signal once
[468](https://docs.rs#468)                    unsafe { first.send(data.take().unwrap()) }
[469](https://docs.rs#469)                    return Ok(true);
[470](https://docs.rs#470)                } else if internal.queue.len() < internal.capacity {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)                    internal.queue.push_back(data.take().unwrap());
[472](https://docs.rs#472)                    return Ok(true);
[473](https://docs.rs#473)                }
[474](https://docs.rs#474)            }
[475](https://docs.rs#475)            Ok(false)
[476](https://docs.rs#476)        }
[477](https://docs.rs#477)
[478](https://docs.rs#478)        /// Returns whether the receive side of the channel is closed or not.
[479](https://docs.rs#479)        ///
[480](https://docs.rs#480)        /// # Examples
[481](https://docs.rs#481)        ///
[482](https://docs.rs#482)        /// ```
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::unbounded::<u64>();
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        /// drop(r); // drop receiver and disconnect the receive side from the channel
[485](https://docs.rs#485)        /// assert_eq!(s.is_disconnected(),true);
[486](https://docs.rs#486)        /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[487](https://docs.rs#487)        /// ```
[488](https://docs.rs#488)        pub fn is_disconnected(&self) -> bool {
[489](https://docs.rs#489)            acquire_internal(&self.internal).recv_count == 0
[490](https://docs.rs#490)        }
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    };
[492](https://docs.rs#492)}
[493](https://docs.rs#493)
[494](https://docs.rs#494)macro_rules! shared_recv_impl {
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    () => {
[496](https://docs.rs#496)        /// Tries receiving from the channel without waiting on the waitlist.
[497](https://docs.rs#497)        /// It returns `Ok(Some(T))` in case of successful operation and
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        /// `Ok(None)` for a failed one, or error in case that channel is
[499](https://docs.rs#499)        /// closed. Important note: this function is not lock-free as it
[500](https://docs.rs#500)        /// acquires a mutex guard of the channel internal for a short time.
[501](https://docs.rs#501)        ///
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        /// # Examples
[503](https://docs.rs#503)        ///
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        /// ```
[505](https://docs.rs#505)        /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[506](https://docs.rs#506)        /// # let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[507](https://docs.rs#507)        /// # let t=spawn(move || {
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        /// #      s.send("Buddy")?;
[509](https://docs.rs#509)        /// #      anyhow::Ok(())
[510](https://docs.rs#510)        /// # });
[511](https://docs.rs#511)        /// loop {
[512](https://docs.rs#512)        ///     if let Some(name)=r.try_recv()?{
[513](https://docs.rs#513)        ///         println!("Hello {}!",name);
[514](https://docs.rs#514)        ///         break;
[515](https://docs.rs#515)        ///     }
[516](https://docs.rs#516)        /// }
[517](https://docs.rs#517)        /// # t.join();
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        /// ```
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        #[inline(always)]
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        pub fn try_recv(&self) -> Result<Option<T>, ReceiveError> {
[522](https://docs.rs#522)            let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[523](https://docs.rs#523)            if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[524](https://docs.rs#524)                return Err(ReceiveError::Closed);
[525](https://docs.rs#525)            }
[526](https://docs.rs#526)            if let Some(v) = internal.queue.pop_front() {
[527](https://docs.rs#527)                if let Some(p) = internal.next_send() {
[528](https://docs.rs#528)                    // if there is a sender take its data and push it into the
[529](https://docs.rs#529)                    // queue Safety: it's safe to receive from owned
[530](https://docs.rs#530)                    // signal once
[531](https://docs.rs#531)                    unsafe { internal.queue.push_back(p.recv()) }
[532](https://docs.rs#532)                }
[533](https://docs.rs#533)                return Ok(Some(v));
[534](https://docs.rs#534)            } else if let Some(p) = internal.next_send() {
[535](https://docs.rs#535)                // Safety: it's safe to receive from owned signal once
[536](https://docs.rs#536)                drop(internal);
[537](https://docs.rs#537)                return unsafe { Ok(Some(p.recv())) };
[538](https://docs.rs#538)            }
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            if internal.send_count == 0 {
[540](https://docs.rs#540)                return Err(ReceiveError::SendClosed);
[541](https://docs.rs#541)            }
[542](https://docs.rs#542)            Ok(None)
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            // if the queue is not empty send the data
[544](https://docs.rs#544)        }
[545](https://docs.rs#545)        /// Tries receiving from the channel without waiting on the waitlist or
[546](https://docs.rs#546)        /// waiting for channel internal lock. It returns `Ok(Some(T))` in case
[547](https://docs.rs#547)        /// of successful operation and `Ok(None)` for a failed one, or error in
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        /// case that channel is closed. Do not use this function unless you
[549](https://docs.rs#549)        /// know exactly what you are doing.
[550](https://docs.rs#550)        ///
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        /// # Examples
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        ///
[553](https://docs.rs#553)        /// ```
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        /// # let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[556](https://docs.rs#556)        /// # let t=spawn(move || {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)        /// #      s.send("Buddy")?;
[558](https://docs.rs#558)        /// #      anyhow::Ok(())
[559](https://docs.rs#559)        /// # });
[560](https://docs.rs#560)        /// loop {
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        ///     if let Some(name)=r.try_recv_realtime()?{
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        ///         println!("Hello {}!",name);
[563](https://docs.rs#563)        ///         break;
[564](https://docs.rs#564)        ///     }
[565](https://docs.rs#565)        /// }
[566](https://docs.rs#566)        /// # t.join();
[567](https://docs.rs#567)        /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[568](https://docs.rs#568)        /// ```
[569](https://docs.rs#569)        #[inline(always)]
[570](https://docs.rs#570)        pub fn try_recv_realtime(&self) -> Result<Option<T>, ReceiveError> {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)            if let Some(mut internal) = try_acquire_internal(&self.internal) {
[572](https://docs.rs#572)                if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[573](https://docs.rs#573)                    return Err(ReceiveError::Closed);
[574](https://docs.rs#574)                }
[575](https://docs.rs#575)                if let Some(v) = internal.queue.pop_front() {
[576](https://docs.rs#576)                    if let Some(p) = internal.next_send() {
[577](https://docs.rs#577)                        // if there is a sender take its data and push it into
[578](https://docs.rs#578)                        // the queue Safety: it's safe to
[579](https://docs.rs#579)                        // receive from owned signal once
[580](https://docs.rs#580)                        unsafe { internal.queue.push_back(p.recv()) }
[581](https://docs.rs#581)                    }
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                    return Ok(Some(v));
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                } else if let Some(p) = internal.next_send() {
[584](https://docs.rs#584)                    // Safety: it's safe to receive from owned signal once
[585](https://docs.rs#585)                    drop(internal);
[586](https://docs.rs#586)                    return unsafe { Ok(Some(p.recv())) };
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                }
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                if internal.send_count == 0 {
[589](https://docs.rs#589)                    return Err(ReceiveError::SendClosed);
[590](https://docs.rs#590)                }
[591](https://docs.rs#591)            }
[592](https://docs.rs#592)            Ok(None)
[593](https://docs.rs#593)        }
[594](https://docs.rs#594)
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        /// Drains all available messages from the channel into the provided vector and returns the number of received messages.
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        ///
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        /// The function is designed to be non-blocking, meaning it only processes messages that are readily available and returns
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        /// immediately with whatever messages are present. It provides a count of received messages, which could be zero if no
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        /// messages are available at the time of the call.
[600](https://docs.rs#600)        ///
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        /// When using this function, it’s a good idea to check if the returned count is zero to avoid busy-waiting in a loop.
[602](https://docs.rs#602)        /// If blocking behavior is desired when the count is zero, you can use the `recv()` function if count is zero. For efficiency,
[603](https://docs.rs#603)        /// reusing the same vector across multiple calls can help minimize memory allocations. Between uses, you can clear
[604](https://docs.rs#604)        /// the vector with `vec.clear()` to prepare it for the next set of messages.
[605](https://docs.rs#605)        ///
[606](https://docs.rs#606)        /// # Examples
[607](https://docs.rs#607)        ///
[608](https://docs.rs#608)        /// ```
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[610](https://docs.rs#610)        /// # let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(1000);
[611](https://docs.rs#611)        /// # let t=spawn(move || {
[612](https://docs.rs#612)        /// #   for i in 0..1000 {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        /// #     s.send(i)?;
[614](https://docs.rs#614)        /// #   }
[615](https://docs.rs#615)        /// #   anyhow::Ok(())
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        /// # });
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        ///
[618](https://docs.rs#618)        /// let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(1000);
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        /// loop {
[620](https://docs.rs#620)        ///     if let Ok(count) = r.drain_into(&mut buf) {
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        ///         if count == 0 {
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        ///            // count is 0, to avoid busy-wait using recv for
[623](https://docs.rs#623)        ///            // the first next message
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        ///            if let Ok(v) = r.recv() {
[625](https://docs.rs#625)        ///               buf.push(v);
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        ///            } else {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        ///              break;
[628](https://docs.rs#628)        ///            }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)        ///         }
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        ///         // use buffer
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        ///         buf.iter().for_each(|v| println!("{}",v));
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        ///     }else{
[633](https://docs.rs#633)        ///         println!("Channel closed");
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        ///         break;
[635](https://docs.rs#635)        ///     }
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        ///     buf.clear();
[637](https://docs.rs#637)        /// }
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        /// # t.join();
[639](https://docs.rs#639)        /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[640](https://docs.rs#640)        /// ```
[641](https://docs.rs#641)        pub fn drain_into(&self, vec: &mut Vec<T>) -> Result<usize, ReceiveError> {
[642](https://docs.rs#642)            let vec_initial_length = vec.len();
[643](https://docs.rs#643)            let remaining_cap = vec.capacity() - vec_initial_length;
[644](https://docs.rs#644)            let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[645](https://docs.rs#645)            if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[646](https://docs.rs#646)                return Err(ReceiveError::Closed);
[647](https://docs.rs#647)            }
[648](https://docs.rs#648)            let required_cap = internal.queue.len() + {
[649](https://docs.rs#649)                if internal.recv_blocking {
[650](https://docs.rs#650)                    0
[651](https://docs.rs#651)                } else {
[652](https://docs.rs#652)                    internal.wait_list.len()
[653](https://docs.rs#653)                }
[654](https://docs.rs#654)            };
[655](https://docs.rs#655)            if required_cap > remaining_cap {
[656](https://docs.rs#656)                vec.reserve(vec_initial_length + required_cap - remaining_cap);
[657](https://docs.rs#657)            }
[658](https://docs.rs#658)            while let Some(v) = internal.queue.pop_front() {
[659](https://docs.rs#659)                vec.push(v);
[660](https://docs.rs#660)            }
[661](https://docs.rs#661)            while let Some(p) = internal.next_send() {
[662](https://docs.rs#662)                // Safety: it's safe to receive from owned signal once
[663](https://docs.rs#663)                unsafe { vec.push(p.recv()) }
[664](https://docs.rs#664)            }
[665](https://docs.rs#665)            Ok(required_cap)
[666](https://docs.rs#666)        }
[667](https://docs.rs#667)
[668](https://docs.rs#668)        /// Returns, whether the send side of the channel, is closed or not.
[669](https://docs.rs#669)        ///
[670](https://docs.rs#670)        /// # Examples
[671](https://docs.rs#671)        ///
[672](https://docs.rs#672)        /// ```
[673](https://docs.rs#673)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::unbounded::<u64>();
[674](https://docs.rs#674)        /// drop(s); // drop sender and disconnect the send side from the channel
[675](https://docs.rs#675)        /// assert_eq!(r.is_disconnected(),true);
[676](https://docs.rs#676)        /// ```
[677](https://docs.rs#677)        pub fn is_disconnected(&self) -> bool {
[678](https://docs.rs#678)            acquire_internal(&self.internal).send_count == 0
[679](https://docs.rs#679)        }
[680](https://docs.rs#680)
[681](https://docs.rs#681)        /// Returns, whether the channel receive side is terminated, and will
[682](https://docs.rs#682)        /// not return any result in future recv calls.
[683](https://docs.rs#683)        ///
[684](https://docs.rs#684)        /// # Examples
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        ///
[686](https://docs.rs#686)        /// ```
[687](https://docs.rs#687)        /// let (s, r) = kanal::unbounded::<u64>();
[688](https://docs.rs#688)        /// s.send(1).unwrap();
[689](https://docs.rs#689)        /// drop(s); // drop sender and disconnect the send side from the channel
[690](https://docs.rs#690)        /// assert_eq!(r.is_disconnected(),true);
[691](https://docs.rs#691)        /// // Also channel is closed from send side, it's not terminated as there is data in channel queue
[692](https://docs.rs#692)        /// assert_eq!(r.is_terminated(),false);
[693](https://docs.rs#693)        /// assert_eq!(r.recv().unwrap(),1);
[694](https://docs.rs#694)        /// // Now channel receive side is terminated as there is no sender for channel and queue is empty
[695](https://docs.rs#695)        /// assert_eq!(r.is_terminated(),true);
[696](https://docs.rs#696)        /// ```
[697](https://docs.rs#697)        pub fn is_terminated(&self) -> bool {
[698](https://docs.rs#698)            let internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[699](https://docs.rs#699)            internal.send_count == 0 && internal.queue.len() == 0
[700](https://docs.rs#700)        }
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    };
[702](https://docs.rs#702)}
[703](https://docs.rs#703)
[704](https://docs.rs#704)impl<T> Sender<T> {
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    /// Sends data to the channel.
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    ///
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    /// # Examples
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    ///
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    /// ```
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// # let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    /// # spawn(move || {
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    ///  s.send("Hello").unwrap();
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    /// #      anyhow::Ok(())
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    /// # });
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// # let name=r.recv()?;
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    /// # println!("Hello {}!",name);
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    /// ```
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    #[inline(always)]
[721](https://docs.rs#721)    pub fn send(&self, data: T) -> Result<(), SendError> {
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[723](https://docs.rs#723)        if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[724](https://docs.rs#724)            let send_count = internal.send_count;
[725](https://docs.rs#725)            // Avoid wasting lock time on dropping failed send object
[726](https://docs.rs#726)            drop(internal);
[727](https://docs.rs#727)            if send_count == 0 {
[728](https://docs.rs#728)                return Err(SendError::Closed);
[729](https://docs.rs#729)            }
[730](https://docs.rs#730)            return Err(SendError::ReceiveClosed);
[731](https://docs.rs#731)        }
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        if let Some(first) = internal.next_recv() {
[733](https://docs.rs#733)            drop(internal);
[734](https://docs.rs#734)            // Safety: it's safe to send to owned signal once
[735](https://docs.rs#735)            unsafe { first.send(data) }
[736](https://docs.rs#736)            Ok(())
[737](https://docs.rs#737)        } else if internal.queue.len() < internal.capacity {
[738](https://docs.rs#738)            // Safety: MaybeUninit is acting like a ManuallyDrop
[739](https://docs.rs#739)            internal.queue.push_back(data);
[740](https://docs.rs#740)            Ok(())
[741](https://docs.rs#741)        } else {
[742](https://docs.rs#742)            let mut data = MaybeUninit::new(data);
[743](https://docs.rs#743)            // send directly to the waitlist
[744](https://docs.rs#744)            let sig = Signal::new_sync(KanalPtr::new_from(data.as_mut_ptr()));
[745](https://docs.rs#745)            internal.push_send(sig.get_terminator());
[746](https://docs.rs#746)            drop(internal);
[747](https://docs.rs#747)            if !sig.wait() {
[748](https://docs.rs#748)                // Safety: data failed to move, sender should drop it if it
[749](https://docs.rs#749)                // needs to
[750](https://docs.rs#750)                if needs_drop::<T>() {
[751](https://docs.rs#751)                    unsafe { data.assume_init_drop() }
[752](https://docs.rs#752)                }
[753](https://docs.rs#753)                return Err(SendError::Closed);
[754](https://docs.rs#754)            }
[755](https://docs.rs#755)            Ok(())
[756](https://docs.rs#756)        }
[757](https://docs.rs#757)        // if the queue is not empty send the data
[758](https://docs.rs#758)    }
[759](https://docs.rs#759)    /// Sends data to the channel with a deadline, if send fails then the object
[760](https://docs.rs#760)    /// will be dropped. you can use send_option_timeout if you like to keep
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    /// the object in case of timeout.
[762](https://docs.rs#762)    ///
[763](https://docs.rs#763)    /// # Examples
[764](https://docs.rs#764)    ///
[765](https://docs.rs#765)    /// ```
[766](https://docs.rs#766)    /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[767](https://docs.rs#767)    /// # use std::time::Duration;
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    /// # let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    /// # spawn(move || {
[770](https://docs.rs#770)    ///  s.send_timeout("Hello",Duration::from_millis(500)).unwrap();
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    /// #      anyhow::Ok(())
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    /// # });
[773](https://docs.rs#773)    /// # let name=r.recv()?;
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    /// # println!("Hello {}!",name);
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    /// ```
[777](https://docs.rs#777)    #[inline(always)]
[778](https://docs.rs#778)    pub fn send_timeout(&self, data: T, duration: Duration) -> Result<(), SendErrorTimeout> {
[779](https://docs.rs#779)        let deadline = Instant::now().checked_add(duration).unwrap();
[780](https://docs.rs#780)        let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[781](https://docs.rs#781)        if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[782](https://docs.rs#782)            let send_count = internal.send_count;
[783](https://docs.rs#783)            // Avoid wasting lock time on dropping failed send object
[784](https://docs.rs#784)            drop(internal);
[785](https://docs.rs#785)            if send_count == 0 {
[786](https://docs.rs#786)                return Err(SendErrorTimeout::Closed);
[787](https://docs.rs#787)            }
[788](https://docs.rs#788)            return Err(SendErrorTimeout::ReceiveClosed);
[789](https://docs.rs#789)        }
[790](https://docs.rs#790)        if let Some(first) = internal.next_recv() {
[791](https://docs.rs#791)            drop(internal);
[792](https://docs.rs#792)            // Safety: it's safe to send to owned signal once
[793](https://docs.rs#793)            unsafe { first.send(data) }
[794](https://docs.rs#794)            Ok(())
[795](https://docs.rs#795)        } else if internal.queue.len() < internal.capacity {
[796](https://docs.rs#796)            // Safety: MaybeUninit is used as a ManuallyDrop, and data in it is
[797](https://docs.rs#797)            // valid.
[798](https://docs.rs#798)            internal.queue.push_back(data);
[799](https://docs.rs#799)            Ok(())
[800](https://docs.rs#800)        } else {
[801](https://docs.rs#801)            let mut data = MaybeUninit::new(data);
[802](https://docs.rs#802)            // send directly to the waitlist
[803](https://docs.rs#803)            let sig = Signal::new_sync(KanalPtr::new_from(data.as_mut_ptr()));
[804](https://docs.rs#804)            internal.push_send(sig.get_terminator());
[805](https://docs.rs#805)            drop(internal);
[806](https://docs.rs#806)            if !sig.wait_timeout(deadline) {
[807](https://docs.rs#807)                if sig.is_terminated() {
[808](https://docs.rs#808)                    // Safety: data failed to move, sender should drop it if it
[809](https://docs.rs#809)                    // needs to
[810](https://docs.rs#810)                    if needs_drop::<T>() {
[811](https://docs.rs#811)                        unsafe { data.assume_init_drop() }
[812](https://docs.rs#812)                    }
[813](https://docs.rs#813)                    return Err(SendErrorTimeout::Closed);
[814](https://docs.rs#814)                }
[815](https://docs.rs#815)                {
[816](https://docs.rs#816)                    let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[817](https://docs.rs#817)                    if internal.cancel_send_signal(&sig) {
[818](https://docs.rs#818)                        return Err(SendErrorTimeout::Timeout);
[819](https://docs.rs#819)                    }
[820](https://docs.rs#820)                }
[821](https://docs.rs#821)                // removing receive failed to wait for the signal response
[822](https://docs.rs#822)                if !sig.wait() {
[823](https://docs.rs#823)                    // Safety: data failed to move, sender should drop it if it
[824](https://docs.rs#824)                    // needs to
[825](https://docs.rs#825)                    if needs_drop::<T>() {
[826](https://docs.rs#826)                        unsafe { data.assume_init_drop() }
[827](https://docs.rs#827)                    }
[828](https://docs.rs#828)                    return Err(SendErrorTimeout::Closed);
[829](https://docs.rs#829)                }
[830](https://docs.rs#830)            }
[831](https://docs.rs#831)            Ok(())
[832](https://docs.rs#832)        }
[833](https://docs.rs#833)        // if the queue is not empty send the data
[834](https://docs.rs#834)    }
[835](https://docs.rs#835)
[836](https://docs.rs#836)    /// Tries to send data from provided option with a deadline, it will panic
[837](https://docs.rs#837)    /// on successful send for None option.
[838](https://docs.rs#838)    ///
[839](https://docs.rs#839)    /// # Examples
[840](https://docs.rs#840)    ///
[841](https://docs.rs#841)    /// ```
[842](https://docs.rs#842)    /// # use std::thread::spawn;
[843](https://docs.rs#843)    /// # use std::time::Duration;
[844](https://docs.rs#844)    /// # let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[845](https://docs.rs#845)    /// # spawn(move || {
[846](https://docs.rs#846)    ///  let mut opt=Some("Hello");
[847](https://docs.rs#847)    ///  s.send_option_timeout(&mut opt,Duration::from_millis(500)).unwrap();
[848](https://docs.rs#848)    /// #      anyhow::Ok(())
[849](https://docs.rs#849)    /// # });
[850](https://docs.rs#850)    /// # let name=r.recv()?;
[851](https://docs.rs#851)    /// # println!("Hello {}!",name);
[852](https://docs.rs#852)    /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[853](https://docs.rs#853)    /// ```
[854](https://docs.rs#854)    #[inline(always)]
[855](https://docs.rs#855)    pub fn send_option_timeout(
[856](https://docs.rs#856)        &self,
[857](https://docs.rs#857)        data: &mut Option<T>,
[858](https://docs.rs#858)        duration: Duration,
[859](https://docs.rs#859)    ) -> Result<(), SendErrorTimeout> {
[860](https://docs.rs#860)        if data.is_none() {
[861](https://docs.rs#861)            panic!("send data option is None");
[862](https://docs.rs#862)        }
[863](https://docs.rs#863)        let deadline = Instant::now().checked_add(duration).unwrap();
[864](https://docs.rs#864)        let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[865](https://docs.rs#865)        if internal.recv_count == 0 {
[866](https://docs.rs#866)            let send_count = internal.send_count;
[867](https://docs.rs#867)            // Avoid wasting lock time on dropping failed send object
[868](https://docs.rs#868)            drop(internal);
[869](https://docs.rs#869)            if send_count == 0 {
[870](https://docs.rs#870)                return Err(SendErrorTimeout::Closed);
[871](https://docs.rs#871)            }
[872](https://docs.rs#872)            return Err(SendErrorTimeout::ReceiveClosed);
[873](https://docs.rs#873)        }
[874](https://docs.rs#874)        if let Some(first) = internal.next_recv() {
[875](https://docs.rs#875)            drop(internal);
[876](https://docs.rs#876)            // Safety: it's safe to send to owned signal once
[877](https://docs.rs#877)            unsafe { first.send(data.take().unwrap()) }
[878](https://docs.rs#878)            Ok(())
[879](https://docs.rs#879)        } else if internal.queue.len() < internal.capacity {
[880](https://docs.rs#880)            internal.queue.push_back(data.take().unwrap());
[881](https://docs.rs#881)            Ok(())
[882](https://docs.rs#882)        } else {
[883](https://docs.rs#883)            // send directly to the waitlist
[884](https://docs.rs#884)            let mut d = data.take().unwrap();
[885](https://docs.rs#885)            let sig = Signal::new_sync(KanalPtr::new_from(&mut d));
[886](https://docs.rs#886)            internal.push_send(sig.get_terminator());
[887](https://docs.rs#887)            drop(internal);
[888](https://docs.rs#888)            if !sig.wait_timeout(deadline) {
[889](https://docs.rs#889)                if sig.is_terminated() {
[890](https://docs.rs#890)                    *data = Some(d);
[891](https://docs.rs#891)                    return Err(SendErrorTimeout::Closed);
[892](https://docs.rs#892)                }
[893](https://docs.rs#893)                {
[894](https://docs.rs#894)                    let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[895](https://docs.rs#895)                    if internal.cancel_send_signal(&sig) {
[896](https://docs.rs#896)                        *data = Some(d);
[897](https://docs.rs#897)                        return Err(SendErrorTimeout::Timeout);
[898](https://docs.rs#898)                    }
[899](https://docs.rs#899)                }
[900](https://docs.rs#900)                // removing receive failed to wait for the signal response
[901](https://docs.rs#901)                if !sig.wait() {
[902](https://docs.rs#902)                    *data = Some(d);
[903](https://docs.rs#903)                    return Err(SendErrorTimeout::Closed);
[904](https://docs.rs#904)                }
[905](https://docs.rs#905)            }
[906](https://docs.rs#906)            Ok(())
[907](https://docs.rs#907)        }
[908](https://docs.rs#908)        // if the queue is not empty send the data
[909](https://docs.rs#909)    }
[910](https://docs.rs#910)    shared_send_impl!();
[911](https://docs.rs#911)    /// Clones [`Sender`] as the async version of it and returns it
[912](https://docs.rs#912)    #[cfg(feature = "async")]
[913](https://docs.rs#913)    pub fn clone_async(&self) -> AsyncSender<T> {
[914](https://docs.rs#914)        let mut internal = acquire_internal(&self.internal);
[915](https://docs.rs#915)        if internal.send_count > 0 {
[916](https://docs.rs#916)            internal.send_count += 1;
[917](https://docs.rs#917)        }
[918](https://docs.rs#918)        drop(internal);
[919](https://docs.rs#919)        AsyncSender::<T> {
[920](https://docs.rs#920)            internal: self.internal.clone(),
[921](https://docs.rs#921)        }
[922](https://docs.rs#922)    }
[923](https://docs.rs#923)
[924](https://docs.rs#924)    /// Converts [`Sender`] to [`AsyncSender`] and returns it
[925](https://docs.rs#925)    /// # Examples
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    ///
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    /// ```
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    /// # tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().unwrap().block_on(async {
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    /// # use tokio::{spawn as co};
[930](https://docs.rs#930)    /// # use std::time::Duration;
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    ///   let (s, r) = kanal::bounded(0);
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    ///   co(async move {
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    ///     let s=s.to_async();
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    ///     s.send("World").await;
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    ///   });
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    ///   let name=r.recv()?;

[938](https://docs.rs#938)    /// # anyhow::Ok(())
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    /// # });
[940](https://docs.rs#940)    /// ```
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    #[cfg(feature = "async")]
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    pub fn to_async(self) -> AsyncSender<T> {
[943](https://docs.rs#943)        // Safety: structure of Sender<T> and AsyncSender<T> is same
[944](https://docs.rs#944)        unsafe { transmute(self) }
[945](https://docs.rs#945)    }
